answer: Each identity tends one trellis row in a garden, locks 80 credits, and files a nectar log with bloom dates and visit counts. An auditor recomputes nectar volume from the bloom table and hive log; a volume error over 5 percent, a reused trellis row, or a copied log burns the bond. The first filing costs 34 and the kth pays 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7027 and 1000 false identities pay 3,530,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-hive ring fails because the hive log binds each row to one garden. An honest identity pays 34 once and recovers its bond after audit.
